evaluation_results.evaluation_name: DigiData: Training and Evaluating General-Purpose Mobile Control Agents

metric_config.evaluation_description: DigiData: Training and Evaluating General-Purpose Mobile Control Agents Standard Accuracy

factsheet.principles_tested: mobile control agents
factsheet.protocol: 1. Given a goal and a trajectory produced by an agent, an LLM judge classifies whether it successfully achieved 2. the goal. We use LLM judges relying on both the screenshot and UI tree.
factsheet.alignment_validation: human operator is asked to judge whether the trajectory successfully achieves the goal or not. Then we assess the alignment between human judge and LLM judge to ensure a high alignment
factsheet.robustness_measures: Prompt variations tested; Multiple runs per sample; Temperature sensitivity tested; Repeated evaluations; Ablation studies; Inter-rater reliability; Significance testing
factsheet.known_limitations: -live and dynamic environment introduces uncontrollable factors (feature deprecation, version changes etc) that makes certain tasks unavailable after a period -sizable efforts required to manually set up prework in the environment

factsheet.principles_tested: Intuitive Physics
factsheet.splits: Debug Set: 60 videos for Model calibration Main Set: 1,012 videos as Main evaluation set Held-Out Set: 344 videos as Test set
factsheet.protocol: Feed a video to the model Ask the model using specific prompts wether the video is physically plausible or not Check if the model's answer match the ground truth label
factsheet.heldout_details: Held-Out Set: 344 videos as Test set
factsheet.alignment_validation: We ran human baselines to ensure that this task is easy for humans.
factsheet.baseline_models: - Human baseline: 96% - Best model baseline: V-JEPA2 56%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Prompt variations tested; Multiple runs per sample; Temperature sensitivity tested
factsheet.known_limitations: Model can be very sensitive to the way they are prompted. Also the compression artefact of the video can also impact the results. Those are mostly limitations on the model sides, since human are not sensitive to those.
factsheet.benchmarks_list: IntPhys: A Framework and Benchmark for Visual Intuitive Physics Reasoning, Riochet et al. 2020

factsheet.principles_tested: Object recognition, Visual categorization, Multi-class classification
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives an image as input 2. Model predicts class label from 1000 classes 3. Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy computed against ground truth
factsheet.heldout_details: Private test set maintained by organizers, used for annual ILSVRC competitions
factsheet.alignment_validation: Expert curation of hierarchical categories, manual verification of labels, consistency checks across similar categories
factsheet.baseline_models: AlexNet: 63.3% top-1 VGG: 71.5% top-1 ResNet-50: 76.1% top-1 ResNet-152: 78.3% top-1 EfficientNet-B7: 84.3% top-1 Human performance: ~95% top-5
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple runs per sample; Significance testing; Inter-rater reliability
factsheet.known_limitations: Class imbalance in some categories; Label noise in training set; Some ambiguous images with multiple valid labels; Bias towards certain object viewpoints and contexts

metric_config.evaluation_description: COCO (Common Objects in Context) Standard Accuracy

factsheet.principles_tested: Object detection, Instance segmentation, Keypoint detection, Panoptic segmentation, Image captioning

factsheet.principles_tested: Complex reasoning, Multi-step thinking, Challenging cognitive tasks, Chain-of-thought reasoning
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives task from one of 23 challenging categories 2. Model generates answer 3. Performance aggregated across all tasks 4. Chain-of-thought prompting typically used
factsheet.alignment_validation: Tasks selected where models underperform humans, difficulty validated through empirical testing
factsheet.baseline_models: PaLM (540B): 56.5% average PaLM (540B) + CoT: 78.1% GPT-4: ~91% Human raters: ~92% average
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple tasks; Chain-of-thought evaluation; Human baseline comparison; Cross-model validation
factsheet.known_limitations: Only 23 tasks (limited coverage); Chain-of-thought prompting required for good performance; Task aggregation methodology; Rapidly saturating with newer models

factsheet.principles_tested: Multi-turn conversation, Instruction following, Reasoning, Writing, Role-playing, Knowledge
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model engages in 2-turn conversation 2. GPT-4 evaluates responses on 10-point scale 3. Scores averaged across turns and categories
factsheet.alignment_validation: Strong correlation with human preferences validated on Chatbot Arena data, GPT-4 judge agreement measured
factsheet.baseline_models: Vicuna-13B: 6.39 GPT-3.5-turbo: 7.94 Claude 2: 8.06 GPT-4: 8.99 GPT-4-turbo: 9.32
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple categories; Position bias mitigation; Agreement with human ratings validated; Pairwise comparison
factsheet.known_limitations: Small dataset (80 questions); GPT-4 judge may have biases; Evaluation cost; Model-based judge limitations; Prompt sensitivity

factsheet.principles_tested: Expert-level knowledge, Scientific reasoning, Domain expertise, Graduate-level understanding
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives graduate-level science question 2. Model selects from 4 multiple choice options 3. Accuracy computed 4. Questions validated to be difficult for non-experts with Google access
factsheet.alignment_validation: PhD-level experts write and validate questions, non-expert validators with Google access achieve <35% accuracy
factsheet.baseline_models: Random: 25% Non-expert w/ Google: 34% Expert: 81% GPT-4: 39% Claude 3 Opus: 59.4% GPT-4o: 53.6%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Expert validation; Non-expert baseline; Multiple subject areas; Quality tiers (Diamond subset)
factsheet.known_limitations: Small dataset size; Limited to 3 scientific domains; Multiple choice format; High cost of expert question creation; Cultural bias toward Western scientific education

factsheet.principles_tested: Instruction following, Constraint satisfaction, Format compliance, Precise control
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives prompt with verifiable instructions (e.g., 'respond in exactly 3 paragraphs', 'include word X at least 5 times') 2. Model generates response 3. Programmatic checks verify instruction compliance 4. Strict and loose accuracy metrics computed
factsheet.alignment_validation: Verifiable instructions with programmatic checking, no ambiguity in correctness
factsheet.baseline_models: GPT-3.5: 57.4% strict GPT-4: 76.9% strict Claude 2: 66.7% strict Gemini Ultra: 79.4% strict
factsheet.robustness_measures: Strict and loose metrics; Multiple instruction types; Programmatic verification; No human evaluation needed
factsheet.known_limitations: Limited to verifiable instructions only; May not reflect realistic usage; Some instructions may be conflicting; Excludes semantic quality assessment
